chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about reciting poetry: does it invalidate wudu (ablution), or a man wronging his companion, or lying? He said: Yes, except if it is poetry in which he speaks truthfully, or it is a small amount of poetry, three or four verses. But as for one who does much false poetry, then it invalidates wudu (ablution).

So the report may bear two possibilities: one of them is that a scribal corruption occurred to the narrator, such that it was narrated with the letter ṣād without a dot rather than ḍād with a dot, because that is among the things that diminish the reward of wudu (ablution). The second is that it is to be understood as recommended.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, meaning an act is considered recommended rather than obligatory
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.ظُلْمِ: wrongdoing or injustice toward another person

ai.seo_question: Does reciting poetry, lying, or ظلم invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses whether reciting poetry, wronging another person, or lying affects wudu (ablution), and it distinguishes between truthful or minimal poetry and excessive false poetry. The closing explanation states that the report may either contain a textual corruption or be understood in the sense of recommendation, indicating that the matter concerns the reward or recommended protection of wudu (ablution).
